newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges slide again.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges slide again.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil barges were weaker on Thursday in lacklustre pre-holiday activity, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded at $110 fob ARA but dealers said this was sold by Esso Netherlands, whose refinery has had problems with a flexi-coking unit, creating an excess of fuel oil. Officials at Esso were not available for comment, and it was not immediately clear for how much longer the unit would still be troubled.
Barge swaps for January were heard traded at $113.75 fob ARA.
While the Esso outage has nudged the front period into a light contango, February lies a couple of dollars in backwardation to January.
High sulphur cargoes were very quiet. One dealer said cif cargo numbers were notionally a dollar or so above barge prices, but no business was heard concluded.
Cargo swaps in the Med were weaker, trading for January at $105.75 fob Med.
Low sulphur prices sagged too, and were traded around $1 a tonne weaker at $124.75. Activity on the physical markets was thin.
